threads.subject: Postmortem: EU API outage on Oct 7 (draft for review)

items.body:
Hi all,

here is the first draft of the postmortem for yesterday's outage. Please read it before Thursday's review and add comments inline in the doc, or reply here if it's quicker.

Summary
Between 07:41 and 08:29 UTC the EU API returned 503 for roughly 38% of requests. The deploy at 07:41 introduced a Cloud SQL proxy sidecar that started after the application container. The app crashed on boot, the readiness probe kept failing and the automatic rollback only covered the first region.

Timeline (UTC)
07:41  r-2026-10-08-0741 rolls out to europe-west3
07:44  automatic rollback in europe-west3 finishes
07:47  europe-west1 picks up the same release from the second wave
07:53  first customer report in #support
08:02  on-call paged (alert fired 6 minutes after threshold)
08:29  manual rollback in europe-west1 finished, error rate back to baseline

Impact
About 41,000 failed requests, 212 affected workspaces, 19 support tickets. No data loss.

Root cause and action items are in the doc. I've left owners blank on purpose so we can decide on Thursday.

Tobias

Thanks Tobias, this reads well. Two things I'd like to understand before Thursday:

1. Why did the alert fire six minutes late? Our SLO burn-rate alert should have caught 38% errors within two minutes.
2. Why did the second wave start at all? I thought the rollout controller halts all waves when any region rolls back.

If (2) is a bug in the controller, I'd rather fix that first than add more probes.
items.quoted:
On Wed, Oct 7, 2026 at 16:05, Tobias Brandt <tobias@habric.com> wrote:
> Hi all,
>
> here is the first draft of the postmortem for yesterday's outage.

items.body:
On (1): the burn-rate alert uses a 5 minute window with a 2 minute "for" clause. With traffic still ramping up after 07:30 the error ratio crossed the threshold at 07:56, not 07:44. So the alert did what it was told, the rule was just too slow for a cold-start morning.

I'd propose a second, faster rule:

```yaml
- alert: ApiErrorBurstEU
  expr: sum(rate(http_requests_total{region=~"europe-.*",code=~"5.."}[1m]))
      / sum(rate(http_requests_total{region=~"europe-.*"}[1m])) > 0.2
  for: 1m
```

On (2) I don't know, Daniel wrote the controller.
items.quoted:
> 1. Why did the alert fire six minutes late?
> 2. Why did the second wave start at all?

items.body:
Customer side: 19 tickets, 3 of them from enterprise accounts with an SLA. Two asked for an RCA in writing. I promised them something by Monday.

Could whoever owns comms make sure the public version doesn't mention the sidecar by name? One of them is evaluating us against a competitor that had a very similar incident last month.

Thanks everyone. My take on owners so we can skip that part on Thursday:

- Startup probe for the SQL proxy: Sofia
- Rollout controller halting all waves on rollback: Daniel
- Faster burn-rate rule (Mara's proposal): Mara
- Written RCA for the three SLA customers: Felix with Emma
- Public status page post-mortem: Emma

Tobias, can you own the doc until it's published? I'd like it out by Friday.
Taking the probe. PR will be up today, it's a five line change plus a test that boots the pod without the proxy.

Found it. The controller does halt all waves, but only for rollbacks it initiated itself. The europe-west3 rollback was triggered by the platform's health check, which the controller sees as a regular new revision. So from its point of view the rollout was still healthy.

Fix: treat any revision change during an active rollout as a halt signal. I'll also add a dry-run mode so we can replay yesterday's event log against the new logic before shipping it.
items.quoted: > Rollout controller halting all waves on rollback: Daniel

items.body:
Draft v2 is up. **Changes:**

- Added Daniel's explanation of the controller behavior to root cause
- Added Mara's alert rule as action item 3
- Owners filled in as Julian proposed
- Customer-facing summary moved to an appendix so Emma can lift it

For the status page I'd go with: "A configuration change in a deployment caused elevated error rates for EU customers between 07:41 and 08:29 UTC. We have rolled back the change and are adding safeguards so that a failing region stops the rollout everywhere."

No sidecar, no vendor names, as Felix asked. Felix, does that work for the SLA customers too or do they need more detail?

Final call: I'll publish v3 internally on Friday at 10:00 unless someone objects. Emma's wording is in, Priya's questions are answered in the root cause section.

Julian, you're the approver on this one.

threads.subject: Invitation: Postmortem review: EU API outage @ Fri 14:00 – 15:00

items.body:
Let's walk through v3 of the postmortem together before it goes out internally on Friday. Timeline, root cause and the follow-ups with owners.

If the slot doesn't work, propose another one.

Hey both,

I wrote up the routing RFC we talked about on Friday. Short version: no folders at all. Every message gets tags from rules, the inbox is just `tag:inbox -tag:done`, and the CLI and the app share the exact same rule engine.

Open questions are at the bottom of the doc. Biggest one: do rules run on the server or on the client?

Mara

Server, definitely. Otherwise the CLI and the app drift the moment someone runs an old binary.

One thing I'd add: rules should be plain text in the repo, so we can review them like code.
items.quoted:
On Mon, Oct 5, 2026 at 09:12, Mara Lindqvist <mara@habric.com> wrote:
> Hey both,
>
> I wrote up the routing RFC we talked about on Friday. Short version: no folders at all.
> Every message gets tags from rules, the inbox is just `tag:inbox -tag:done`.
>
> Mara

items.body:
+1 on server-side and rules in the repo. I'd keep a dry-run mode in the CLI though: `mailcli rules test --since 7d` should show which tags *would* change before we deploy a rule.

Can we also get rid of "archive"? Archive is just removing `inbox`.
items.quoted:
> Server, definitely. Otherwise the CLI and the app drift the moment someone runs an old binary.

Agreed, that's the whole point.

items.body:
Dry-run is in. I also added `mailcli rules diff` that prints the tag delta per thread, works nicely with `less`.

Archive = `-inbox`: yes, I'll update the section on keyboard shortcuts so `e` maps to that.

Ran the dry-run against my last 30 days: 2,184 threads, 31 tag changes, all of them look right except newsletters from GitHub that also match `tag:review`.

Julian, can you sign off on the RFC today so I can start the migration on Monday? The only thing left is your call on the rate limit for rule evaluation (I'd say 50 rules / account).

threads.subject: [zed-industries/zed] gpui: measure list items against available width (#40211)

items.body:
@ninaokafor requested your review on this pull request.

List items without an explicit width were measured with a min-content constraint, which made rows shrink-wrap their children. This passes the list's width as a definite available space.

@ninaokafor commented on this pull request.

Added a test that reproduces the shrink-wrapped rows from your report: it renders a list whose items have no explicit width inside a 400px container and asserts the row bounds match the container.

While doing that I noticed uniform_list had the same problem when the first item is measured, so I fixed it there too. That one is a separate commit in case you want to review it on its own.

Mind taking another look? CI is green on macOS and Linux.

threads.subject: Staff Engineer, Rust / GPU rendering (remote, EU)

items.body:
Hi Julian,

I came across your work on GPUI-based tooling and wanted to reach out. I'm helping a Berlin-based devtools company (about 40 people, Series B, profitable) find a Staff Engineer for their rendering team.

What they're working on: a native, GPU-accelerated editor for data pipelines. The core is Rust, the UI layer is their own retained-mode toolkit and they are considering moving parts of it to GPUI. You'd own the text layout and rendering stack.

Remote in the EU, two on-sites per quarter, salary band 120–145k plus equity.

Would you be open to a 20 minute call next week? Happy to share more details on the team first if that's easier.

Best,
Lena
